evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.

After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

Ravenous Hydra / Tiamat '{{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}', Blade of the Ruined King '{{rd|9%|6%}}', Titanic Hydra '{{rd|4%|2%}}' -> first argument is the melee value, second the ranged value. Hence Expose Weakness = 8% melee / 5% ranged.

Black Cleaver: 40 AD, 400 health, 20 ability haste (no attack speed, no lethality, no crit). Bloodsong: 200 health, 9 gold/10, 75% health+mana regen (no AD, no AS, no ability haste, no lethality). Neither item carries any stat that scales a per-hit damage number by 8.33%.

Black Cleaver average stacks (ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction): the established model uses a fixed 0.8*max_stacks constant (with a hits/2 short-fight branch) ... the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes.

N(T) = floor(AS * u * T)  (damage.py: num_auto_attacks = floor(...)) ... a swing whose impact would land *exactly* at the window boundary is excluded, a measure-zero boundary choice. ... Uptime as a rate scale ... The error is bounded by +/-1 swing and vanishes as T grows.
Only one damage-amplification keystone text exists in the cache: '... bonus adaptive damage and grant you 8% increased damage against champions ...'. No cached amp constant equals 8.33%.

step_1_exact_ratio.rounding_band: Both leaves are displayed to 1 decimal, so the true ratio lies in [300.25/277.25, 300.35/277.15] = [1.08296, 1.08371]. 13/12 = 1.08333 sits inside; any candidate outside this band is excluded.

step_2_exclude_bloodsong_amp.conclusion: The diff is NOT 'Expose Weakness started (or stopped) applying' and is not a melee/ranged fix of the amp.

step_3_exclude_amp_merge_rules.work: Merging two amps a,b: multiplicative/additive = (1+a)(1+b)/(1+a+b); for the only cached amp constants (8% item, 8% keystone, 5% ranged) this gives 1.0055 (8%+8%) or 1.0030 (8%+5%) - far below the band. 'Largest-only' -> 'both multiplied' gives exactly (1 + smaller amp) = 1.08 or 1.05 - also outside the band. Reaching 1.08333 by an amp-merge rule would require a cached amplifier of exactly 8.333%, which does not exist (S4, S8).
step_3_exclude_amp_merge_rules.conclusion: No amplification-merge rule over the cached constants can produce 13/12.

step_4_exclude_black_cleaver_stack_model.work: With m(R)=100/(100+R) (S6) and Carve shred r on base armor A, ratio = (100 + A(1-r_old)) / (100 + A(1-r_new)). Solving = 13/12: r 0.24 -> 0.30 (the 0.8*max_stacks constant -> full 5 stacks of S5/S1) requires A = 5000 armor; the asymptotic maximum of that change as A -> infinity is 0.76/0.70 = 1.0857, and at a realistic A = 100 it is only 176/170 = 1.0353. The Cesaro-mean correction of S5 moves the stack count by at most one stack (6% armor), which at A = 100 is a 1.7% damage change.
step_4_exclude_black_cleaver_stack_model.conclusion: A Black Cleaver stack-model change cannot move a mitigated damage total by 8.33% at any realistic armor. (For completeness, 'shred absent -> shred present' would need A = 34.48 for 30% or A = 47.17 for 24% - unverifiable without the scenario roster, and it would also require the per-hit value to change, which step 5 shows it did not.)

step_5_decomposition_that_does_fit.work: 277.2 = 12 * 23.1 and 300.3 = 13 * 23.1 exactly. Dividing out the ranged Expose Weakness amp of S2/S3: 277.2/1.05 = 264.0 = 12 * 22 and 300.3/1.05 = 286.0 = 13 * 22 - both exact integers, i.e. a per-instance post-mitigation 22.0 amplified to 23.1. The per-instance number is IDENTICAL on both sides of the diff (23.1); only the instance count changed, 12 -> 13.
step_5_decomposition_that_does_fit.conclusion: The whole diff is one additional damage instance on an otherwise byte-identical mitigation/amplification chain. No item constant (6%/stack, 5 stacks, 30% cap, 100% base AD, 8%/5% amp, 1.5 s / 4 s / 6 s / 10 s timers) is violated by either value.

step_6_which_count_is_right.work: Per S7 the count is governed by N(T) = floor(AS*u*T) with interior swings counted and a swing landing exactly at T excluded (for casts: a cast counts when it STARTS inside the window). A +/-1 swing difference is precisely the tolerance S7 attaches to the uptime-as-rate-scale model. Certifying 12 vs 13 in absolute terms requires the scenario's attack speed, uptime and fight window (and, in a coupled roster, the participant's death time) - these live in the golden scenario definition under scripts/, which this runbook forbids reading, and they are not present anywhere in data/ (grep for 'cleaver_bloodsong' across the whole export returns nothing; data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json has no Cleaver/Bloodsong scenario).
step_6_which_count_is_right.conclusion: The absolute count could not be derived from the permitted evidence. The wiki-derived verdict is therefore a consistency verdict, not an absolute recomputation.

independent_computation.verdict_rationale: Everything wiki-checkable is unchanged between the two values: the per-instance damage 23.1 (= 22.0 post-mitigation * 1.05 ranged Expose Weakness) is identical, so the mitigation order, the Carve shred, the Spellblade base-AD row and the amplification chain all reproduce identically under both. The diff is exactly +1 damage instance (x13/12), which no Black Cleaver or Bloodsong constant can fabricate and which no amp-merge rule can produce - it is a counting/timing effect inside the documented +/-1-swing band of docs/math-foundations.md S1.1. Since no cached wiki value contradicts the new number, and the new number preserves every constant the old one honored while adding a swing that the documented floor(AS*u*T) convention counts (interior swings all count; only a swing landing exactly at T is dropped), the new value is the one consistent with the stated convention. Flagged: this is a consistency verdict at low-moderate confidence, NOT an absolute recomputation - an over-counted boundary swing would produce the same +1 signature in the opposite direction, and distinguishing the two requires the scenario's AS/uptime/window, which is outside the permitted evidence tree.
